To clarify:

My wife was bitten by a dog on the back of her ankle over a year ago. The little puncture wounds healed fine but left scars. Ever since then, the scars will randomly start to itch, especially after a hot shower (that's like a regular shower, except I'm in it with her... Sorry, I couldn't resist). She says that scratching doesn't help because the itch is "under" the surface where she can't get to it. What could be causing that?
Why do scars get itchy under the surface?

Tl;dr- chemicals (histamines) cause itching when your body thinks it is hurt.

I'll give this a shot, though I'm not sure it is 100% correct in your wife's situation.

Out of curiosity, does this also happen after/during exercise? What about after being on her feet all day?

When your body is damaged it releases chemokines, cytokines, histamines, and other timey wimey mumbo jumbo body stuff in order to recruit white blood cells to the site of injury to slow blood flow, decrease your pain threshold, kill microbes, "eat" dead tissue, and cause inflammation and itchiness. This prevents wound infiltrates from spreading and keeps the damage localized. This is also why anti-histamines relieve itching and swelling.

That being said, it sounds like she was bitten on her Achilles tendon (back of ankle) which may take a while to heal. This is because it receives a lot of stress when walking or running (especially your mom's). If we assume that it is constantly being mildly "reinjured" throughout the day those chemicals are probably being released to try and prevent the spread of the perceived external injury. On top of all this is a hot shower which causes mild swelling which may provoke a stronger response at the injury.

The injury occurred over a year ago so her tendons should be all healed but may have healed too tight, too loose, or might possibly have formed little tiny adhesions (Google it). But probably not the adhesions, I'm just throwing possibilities out there.

Scars on the skin form when the fiber mesh work in the skin heals along a line, making the skin somewhat inflexible (or less flexible). It could be that in the hot water her ankle swells slightly and causes the skin to get uncomfortably tight along the scars. That could stimulate a release of those chemicals in order to recruit WBCs to fix the supposed injury.

See if ice will make the itching go away. If not ice then benadryl. If not that then some NSAID like ibuprofen or aleve. If not those then try RICE- Rest Ice Compression Elevation. If not any of that then tell her to deal with it.

Fin.
